- When sentiment is negative in the recent history, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if recent sentiment is negative.
- If model shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive high forecasts) and sentiment is positive, check for overshoot; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high if sentiment remains positive.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model often overestimates continuation; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–5 days post-spike if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in the 3–5 day window following sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period if sentiment is positive; apply 2–5% downward adjustment for first 7–10 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment, model often underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is negative for 3+ consecutive days.
